item.aggregated_output: /home/ryan/work/code/personal/taryx M docs/project/evidence/verdict.schema.json ?? docs/project/evidence/m1/m1-events-r1.jsonl ?? docs/project/evidence/m1/m1-session-bootstrap.md # Taryx documentation guide Created: 2026-10-25 Scope: Project planning, task tracking, decisions, verification evidence, and work records in Taryx. ## Purpose and source of truth Use Markdown to preserve what we intend to build, what is agreed, what comes next, what is blocked, and what has actually been verified. This workflow adapts Cateniq's conventions to Taryx's single-repository boundary. Taryx owns its records independently; Cateniq and Voltix are references, not shared trackers. Canonical documents live in `docs/project/`, relative to the Taryx root. The repository README is the entry point. Do not maintain another project README or duplicate backlog elsewhere. If preserved locally, `docs/initial-discussion/` files are background discussions and proposals. The original planning chats currently live outside this repository; the README and canonical planning records capture the reconciled direction without depending on those local files. Preserve them as source material. Their titles, including “Final,” do not establish current acceptance. During planning, reconcile them with the user's agreements and later review findings, then link from the canonical specifications. Do not silently promote every suggestion into an accepted requirement. ## File layout and ownership ```text README.md Introduction, verified setup, documentation links AGENTS.md Scoped agent workflow instructions .devin/skills/project-management/ Portable project-management skill docs/initial-discussion/ Preserved background proposals and conversations docs/agent-notes/ Tooling notes and agent workarounds (non-canonical) docs/project/ documentation-guide.md Process, templates, and record ownership roadmap.md Milestones, scope, dependencies, exit criteria backlog.md Canonical task records and status architecture.md Current design and acceptance/implementation status blockers.md Obstacles and unresolved decision gates features/*.md Behaviour and acceptance specifications, when needed decisions/001-short-title.md Significant decisions and their reasoning evidence// Sanitised verification findings, when needed journal/YYYY-MM.md Historical work outcomes and verification ``` The root `README.md` preserves motivation, portfolio context and source links. Canonical architecture, feature contracts and task records own evolving implementation details; link to them rather than maintaining a second plan in the concept document. Create feature specifications and evidence documents only when they have useful content. This setup does not require empty future directories or a preselected implementation backlog. | Record | Owns | Update when | | --- | --- | --- | | `README.md` | Introduction, setup, navigation | Setup or documentation locations change; do not duplicate task status here | | `documentation-guide.md` | Workflow and templates | The process or tracking ownership changes | | `roadmap.md` | Milestone scope, dependencies, exit criteria, progress | Scope or sequence changes, work begins, or exit criteria pass | | `backlog.md` | Task IDs, priorities, status, acceptance and completion evidence | Work is refined, started, blocked, completed, reopened, or dropped | | `architecture.md` | Boundaries, components, interfaces, persistence and deployment design | Design is accepted or implementation changes it | | `blockers.md` | Questions, impact, evidence, unblock actions and resolutions | An obstacle is identified, investigated, or resolved | | `features/*.md` | Behaviour, inputs, outputs, rules, failure cases and acceptance | Before implementation and when agreed behaviour changes | | `decisions/*.md` | Context, choice, alternatives, consequences and acceptance source | A significant choice is proposed, accepted, rejected, or superseded | | `evidence//` | Reproducible checks, observations and limitations | Verification needs detail beyond a task's short completion evidence | | `journal/YYYY-MM.md` | Dated outcomes, checks, model/agent attribution | A meaningful work unit concludes or reaches a useful partial outcome | Prefer links over repeated explanations. Task status belongs in tasks, milestone status in the roadmap, reasoning in decisions, and historical outcomes in the journal. ## Roadmap conventions Taryx milestones live in the roadmap and are established through project planning. Do not copy Cateniq's or Voltix's milestones or automatically adopt the sequence in an initial discussion document. For each agreed milestone record: - Outcome and included scope. - Exclusions and dependencies. - Observable exit criteria and linked tasks/evidence. - Status: `Planned`, `In progress`, or `Complete`. Detail the upcoming milestone and immediate dependencies; keep later work broad. Mark completion only when exit criteria are satisfied. Distinguish local verification, hosted CI, native service verification, and release readiness where relevant. If a gate is deferred, explicitly record the accepted scope change and follow-up; do not silently claim it passed. ## Task records Initially keep task bodies in `backlog.md`. Assign sequential IDs starting at `TAR-001`; never reuse an ID. IDs identify tasks, not priority. Maintain a compact index in ascending ID order, using a leading status icon and a link to each task. Append new task links at the end. Task sections own the status word; index icons mirror it. Put delivery order and next-work context in `Delivery notes`, not in index ordering. Use explicit anchors for stable links: ```markdown ## TAR-XXX — Short outcome-oriented title - Repository: taryx - Area: documentation | workspace | metering | pricing | billing | migration | integration | portal | verification | deployment - Milestone: agreed milestone, or Not assigned - Priority: High | Normal | Low - Status: Backlog 📋 | Ready 🟢 | In progress 🚧 | Blocked ⛔ | Done ✅ | Dropped 🗑️ - Depends on: task IDs, or None - References: specification and decision links ### Outcome Describe the concrete deliverable or behaviour. ### Done when - Observable acceptance criterion. - Relevant verification requirement. ### Completion evidence Actual checks and results, including failures or checks not run. Link commits/PRs when known. Otherwise identify changed files and uncommitted state. ### Notes Material context, blocker link, next action, or reason for reopening/dropping. ``` | State | Icon | Meaning | | --- | --- | --- | | Backlog | 📋 | Identified work needing refinement or prioritisation | | Ready | 🟢 | Scope and acceptance are clear; dependencies satisfied | | In progress | 🚧 | Actively underway; keep the active set small | | Blocked | ⛔ | A specific obstacle prevents progress; link its blocker | | Done | ✅ | Acceptance and required verification satisfied, with evidence | | Dropped | 🗑️ | Removed from scope deliberately, with a recorded reason | Write the icon after the status word in task sections, for example `Status: Done ✅`. Update the index icon whenever status changes. Several status icons are non-BMP (4-byte UTF-8) characters that the file-edit tools corrupt on write; apply icon changes with scripted writes and verify the bytes per [the emoji-corruption note](../agent-notes/emoji-corruption.md). Prefer tasks reviewable in a focused session. Split by meaningful outcome, not file count. Retain completed records. Required verification pending means the task is not Done. Reopen with a reason or create a follow-up for new scope. Minor edits need not manufacture a task. If the backlog becomes unwieldy, move bodies to `tasks/TAR-XXX-short-title.md` and retain the backlog as an index. Preserve IDs and links; do not maintain duplicate bodies. ## Blockers and open questions Use sequential stable IDs such as `BLK-001`. Record: - Identification date and the concrete question or obstacle. - Status: `Open` or `Resolved`. - Affected tasks/milestones and practical impact. - Whether it blocks current work or can be investigated alongside it. - Evidence, attempted approaches, and relevant links. - Next action and who or what can resolve it. - Resolution and date when resolved. Do not mark the whole project blocked because one task is blocked. Future planning decisions are not failed implementation attempts. Keep evidence and resolution here; tasks link to them. Record a lasting design choice in a decision record when warranted. ## Decision records Use numbered files such as `001-markdown-project-tracking.md` for material architecture, correctness, scope, or maintenance choices. Routine implementation details do not require a decision record. Each record contains title, date, status (`Proposed`, `Accepted`, `Rejected`, `Superseded`), context, decision, alternatives, consequences, follow-up, and relevant links. Accepted records must identify their acceptance source: explicit user agreement or a selection within delegated authority. Recommendations alone are not acceptance. When replacing a decision, preserve its original reasoning, mark it Superseded, and link to its replacement. Update the current specification or architecture separately. Accepted design is not proof of implementation or verification. ## Verification evidence Record the command or procedure, environment, inputs/workload, observed result, and limitations. Link detailed findings from the affected task when useful. Distinguish passing, failing, skipped, and unavailable checks. Keep synthetic/simulated results distinct from hardware observations, and local results distinct from hosted CI or deployment results. Do not claim guarantees broader than the evidence. Keep secrets and unsanitised sensitive responses out of all records. Avoid committing bulky generated outputs when a concise reproducible procedure and findings suffice. ## Session workflow ### Before work 1. Read this guide, roadmap, and backlog to identify the current outcome and next task. 2. Read relevant specifications, architecture sections, decisions, and blockers. 3. Inspect actual files and repository state; documentation may lag. 4. Confirm acceptance criteria/dependencies and mark the task In progress when beginning it. ### During work 1. Stay within the authorised scope; record useful newly discovered work separately. 2. Update specifications when agreed behaviour changes. 3. Record material decisions, blockers, and actual verification results. 4. Preserve unrelated changes. When several agents contribute, coordinate task/file ownership and reconcile their evidence before marking the overall task Done. ### Before ending meaningful work 1. Update affected tasks with status, evidence, remaining work, and the next action. 2. Update affected architecture/specifications and blockers. 3. Change milestone status only when its exit criteria warrant it. 4. Add one concise journal entry for the work unit, or amend its existing entry. 5. Check links, status/index consistency, and contradictions across changed records. Apply this after implementation, substantive investigation, accepted planning decisions, or documentation deliverables without a separate reminder. Pure explanations and unchanged status checks need no edits. Documentation closeout does not trigger another journal entry about itself. When an authorised commit occurs, include related records in the same commit as the change they describe. Record changed files or a branch/PR in the journal rather than trying to include its own commit SHA. Reserve standalone `Records:` commits for record-only corrections. This workflow does not itself authorise commits, pushes, external tracker changes, publication, or scheduled automation. ### At milestone boundaries Review exit criteria, evidence, outstanding tasks, and blockers. Mark completion only when supported, then refine the next milestone. Preserve explicit verification gaps rather than describing local completion as release readiness. ## Journal format and time Use monthly files named for the UTC entry date. Read the system clock, for example `date -u`, rather than estimating or converting local time manually. Journal headings use `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC`. Ordinary planning dates may use the user's local date (Australia/Sydney); label times explicitly when ambiguity matters. ```markdown ## YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC — Short work outcome - LLM model: Reliable session-reported model; note unknown variant details. - Coding agent: Agent/application; version only if known. - Tasks: TAR-XXX, or None for work without a task. - Completed: Concrete outcome or meaningful partial result. - Verification: Checks performed and actual outcomes, including limitations. - Remaining: Next action or links to unfinished tasks/blockers. - Changes: Commit/PR references, or changed files if uncommitted. ``` Every entry includes separate LLM model and coding agent fields. Do not infer model identity from the agent name, available-model lists, or defaults. If only the family is known, record it and say the exact variant is unavailable. Use `Unknown (not recorded)` where no reliable evidence exists. List multiple contributors and their roles when relevant. Keep entries short; do not copy transcripts or entire acceptance checklists. Correct factual errors without erasing the history of what was known at the time. Do not duplicate this journal in another location. ## Maintenance The project-root `AGENTS.md` activates this workflow through the `project-management` skill, with a repository-carried copy at `.devin/skills/project-management/SKILL.md`. If it is unavailable, read this guide and restore the repository copy; do not introduce machine-local dependencies. It is a session routine, not a background watcher. Reconcile interrupted work at the next session. Update only affected records. Preserve discussion sources and completed history. If an external tracker is adopted later, migrate task ownership and stop maintaining a second Markdown task tracker; retain specifications, architecture, decisions, and operational documentation in the repository and update this guide. --- name: project-management description: Maintain Taryx's Markdown roadmap, tasks, decisions, blockers, and work journal per docs/project/documentation-guide.md. Use for meaningful Taryx work and after implementation, investigation, planning decisions, or documentation updates. allowed-tools: - read - grep - glob - edit - exec --- # Project management and documentation Keep Taryx's durable project records aligned with actual work. This is an in-session workflow, not a background watcher or scheduled task. ## Establish the source of truth - Read the root `AGENTS.md` instructions and `docs/project/documentation-guide.md`. The guide owns record locations, templates, task/blocker formats, statuses, timezone, and update rules — follow it exactly. - Read only the roadmap, active tasks, and specifications/decisions relevant to the work. Reconcile records with code, verification output, and the current conversation. - Treat `docs/initial-discussion/` as preserved background proposals. Their titles and embedded suggestions do not establish acceptance; reconcile them with user agreements and link them from canonical records. - Inspect actual files and repository state before updating records; documentation may lag reality. ## Update after meaningful work Before the final response following implementation, a substantive investigation, an accepted planning decision, or a documentation deliverable: 1. Update the affected task in `docs/project/backlog.md` with actual status, completion evidence, remaining work, and the next concrete action. Reuse its `TAR-XXX` ID. Add a task for newly identified work only when useful under the guide's conventions; do not invent historical IDs or manufacture a ticket for every minor edit. 2. Update feature specifications for changed behaviour and `docs/project/architecture.md` for changed technical design. Keep proposed, accepted, implemented, and verified states distinct; recommendations are not acceptance. 3. Record material obstacles and unresolved questions in `docs/project/blockers.md` with affected tasks, impact, evidence, and an unblock action. Resolve existing records when evidence supports it. 4. Update milestone status in `docs/project/roadmap.md` only when its exit criteria warrant it. Preserve agreed scope and sequencing. 5. Add one concise journal entry for the completed work unit or meaningful partial outcome in `docs/project/journal/YYYY-MM.md`, following the guide's format. Include verification performed, limitations, and task/commit/PR links when available. Mark uncommitted work honestly. Read the system clock (`date -u`) for the UTC timestamp and record LLM model and coding agent as separate fields; write `Unknown (not recorded)` rather than guessing. 6. Check consistency and references among affected files. Briefly mention material documentation updates in the final response. Update only affected records. If an answer is purely explanatory, a status check reveals no change, or the same outcome has already been recorded, make no documentation edit. If repeating this workflow for the same work unit, amend the existing entry rather than append a duplicate. Documentation updates do not themselves trigger another round of journaling. ## Evidence and scope - A task is Done only when acceptance criteria and required verification are satisfied. Report failed, skipped, or unavailable checks; do not claim that a commit, deployment, or test occurred without evidence. - Keep status in the backlog, milestone progress in the roadmap, reasoning in decisions, and historical outcomes in the journal. Prefer links to duplicate explanations. - Preserve completed records and decision history. Supersede outdated decisions rather than silently rewriting their original reasoning. - Do not overwrite unrelated work, bootstrap every missing document during routine closeout, or rewrite the backlog based on guesses. If a required record cannot be updated, state the specific limitation and next action. - Status icons and other non-BMP characters are corrupted by the `edit`/`write` tools; apply those changes with scripted writes and verify the bytes — see `docs/agent-notes/emoji-corruption.md`. - This workflow does not authorise commits, pushes, messages, external tracker mutations, or scheduled automations. Preserve the user's existing authorisation scope.

item.aggregated_output: c88b722f30526d8c57aef7ff89634ecd8a1fa983 /bin/bash: line 1: rg: command not found # Taryx roadmap Date: 2026-10-25 This is the initial delivery sequence, not a calendar commitment. The earlier 6–10 week ambition is a sizing hypothesis; reassess after M1 and M3. [Backlog](backlog.md) owns task status; [architecture](architecture.md) owns design. M1 is complete after remediation of the independent exit review findings. | Milestone | Outcome | Status | Depends on | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Documentation setup | Portable Cateniq-style workflow | Complete | None | | Planning baseline | Architecture, feature contracts and evidence-driven backlog | Complete | Documentation setup | | M1 — Foundation and domain profile | Reproducible workspace, sourced profile and metering history | Complete | Planning baseline | | M2 — Explainable bills and corrections | End-to-end operator billing with financial integrity | Complete | M1 | | M3 — Safe legacy migration | Characterisation, shadow comparison and controlled cohort cutover | In progress | M2 | | M4 — Client variation and market boundary | Second isolated client and bounded integration | Planned | M3 | | M5 — Operational portfolio delivery | Recovery evidence, Kubernetes and reproducible demonstration | Planned | M4 | Setup and planning completion refer only to [TAR-001](backlog.md#tar-001) and [TAR-002](backlog.md#tar-002). Core product value is demonstrated at M3; M4 and M5 extend it. Changes to that scope require an explicit record, not silent omission of unfinished extensions. ## M1 — Foundation and domain profile Independent review at `b5a180f` reopened TAR-004/TAR-005 for format compatibility and ingestion correctness; all five findings remediated and all ten preserved probes now pass. See [review](evidence/m1/m1-exit-review.md). Scope: TAR-003–005. Create a locked Python/Django/Graphene/Celery and React workspace, real PostgreSQL/RabbitMQ Compose environment, import contracts, minimal CI configuration, frozen supported metering/tariff/time profile and deterministic fixtures with revision ingestion. Dependencies: TAR-003 may start now. TAR-004 uses the bootstrap environment to freeze numeric/reference and workload gates; source research can begin earlier. TAR-005 requires both. Exit criteria: - A clean checkout can install locked dependencies, start the skeleton and run smoke/import-boundary checks. - Supported format subset, quality/revision precedence, units, time boundaries and rounding are sourced and frozen with independent expected cases. - Duplicate/corrected/conflicting batches preserve history and deterministic current selection in PostgreSQL. - Workload and performance acceptance budgets are recorded against the reference environment. Excludes issuance, ledger, migration and Kubernetes. Gates: [BLK-001](blockers.md#blk-001), [BLK-003](blockers.md#blk-003). ## M2 — Explainable bills and corrections Independent re-review at `de0e08d` reopened TAR-006/TAR-009 for incomplete rating evidence and account-scoped recovery; all four follow-up findings remediated and both preserved probes pass. See the [review](evidence/m2/m2-independent-review.md). Independent review at `2a46650` reopened TAR-006–009 for financial/input integrity and browser/retry failures; all seven findings remediated and the six preserved probes now pass alongside a 102-test suite and a live CSRF-origin-verified portal journey. See [review](evidence/m2/m2-independent-review.md). Re-review of the residual readiness gaps it lists (itemised portal explanation, real broker-fault timing, after-commit/ack kill, bounded query behaviour) remains open evidence work. Scope: TAR-006–009. Rating engine, durable admission/outbox, atomic invoice/ledger issuance, successive revision adjustments and an authenticated operator journey. Exit criteria: - Itemised calculations match independent references under the frozen profile. - Unique business identities, transactional posting and journal enforcement survive concurrent duplicate requests. - Repeated and successive meter corrections adjust the net recognised liability without changing issued history. - Operator import/bill/explain/correct workflow works through the real API, including permission and stale-input errors. - Broker interruption leaves admitted work recoverable; no false completion is shown. Excludes legacy cutover, a second client and external market integration. Full process-fault and performance campaigns mature in M5, but tests necessary to establish financial correctness cannot be deferred. ## M3 — Safe legacy migration Current verdict: Complete. The last F2 commit-window race is remediated — the commit-window probe and all 13 preserved M3 probes pass; see the [third remediation addendum](evidence/m3/m3-independent-review.md#third-remediation-addendum--2026-10-25). Earlier verdicts below are historical. Scope: TAR-010–012. Independent legacy calculator, fictional policy/defect fixtures, shadow isolation, versioned comparison evidence and operator cutover. Exit criteria (verified — see [implementer review](evidence/m3/m3-exit-review.md) and the remediated [independent review](evidence/m3/m3-independent-review.md)): - Legacy and new engines compare equivalent snapshots, detecting line differences even when totals match. - Shadow attempts cannot write financial records; inconclusive results block evidence. - Operator preserves a historical policy and approves a scoped legacy-defect correction. - Stale approvals, concurrent route changes and in-flight issuance cannot bypass cutover gates. - The cohort journey from legacy to new is reproducible, audited and visible in the portal. Excludes migration of an entire historical accounting database. Routing rollback concerns future operations only. ## M4 — Client variation and market boundary Scope: TAR-013–015. Same-image isolated retailers, sourced or explicitly synthetic market workflow, durable adapter and deterministic counterparty simulator. Exit criteria: - Client policies differ as intended without cross-client imports, data access or queue access. - Market transition/protocol profile and limits are frozen before implementation. - Duplicate, delayed, out-of-order and rejected messages recover or fail according to the transition table. - Adapter restart and uncertain outcomes reconcile without duplicate business transitions; unrelated billing remains available. Excludes full MSATS/aseXML conformance and live AEMO connectivity. Gate: [BLK-002](blockers.md#blk-002). ## M5 — Operational portfolio delivery Scope: TAR-016–018. Correlated diagnostics, process-fault campaign, kind deployment, migration/rollout safety, measured workloads and presentation. Exit criteria: - Required [verification scenarios](features/verification.md) have reproducible evidence with no undisclosed failures/skips. - Forced worker termination before/after commit, outbox interruptions and broker recovery preserve financial invariants. - Fresh Kubernetes installation, compatible schema migration and failed rollout are demonstrated with explicit availability limits. - Resource use, throughput/latency and recovery meet the frozen local budgets, or a documented scope revision is accepted. - Another developer can follow tested setup/reset/demo instructions; a recording and explanation show the full journey and limitations. Local completion does not imply green hosted CI, cloud deployment or production regulatory readiness. Report each separately. Public hosting, AWS/Terraform/ArgoCD and a second territory remain future candidates. # Taryx backlog Updated: 2026-10-25 Task sections own status; index icons mirror them. See the [documentation guide](documentation-guide.md#task-records). ## Task index - ✅ [TAR-001 — Establish project-management standards](#tar-001) - ✅ [TAR-002 — Establish the planning baseline](#tar-002) - ✅ [TAR-003 — Bootstrap the development workspace](#tar-003) - ✅ [TAR-004 — Freeze domain and measurement profiles](#tar-004) - ✅ [TAR-005 — Implement versioned meter ingestion and fixtures](#tar-005) - ✅ [TAR-006 — Implement deterministic itemised rating](#tar-006) - ✅ [TAR-007 — Implement durable issuance and balanced posting](#tar-007) - ✅ [TAR-008 — Implement successive corrections and adjustments](#tar-008) - ✅ [TAR-009 — Deliver the core operator journey](#tar-009) - ✅ [TAR-010 — Build independent legacy characterisation](#tar-010) - ✅ [TAR-011 — Implement isolated shadow comparison and gates](#tar-011) - ✅ [TAR-012 — Deliver operator migration and cutover](#tar-012) - 📋 [TAR-013 — Demonstrate two isolated client instances](#tar-013) - 📋 [TAR-014 — Freeze the bounded market workflow](#tar-014) - 📋 [TAR-015 — Implement market adapter and counterparty simulator](#tar-015) - 📋 [TAR-016 — Verify recovery and correlated diagnostics](#tar-016) - 📋 [TAR-017 — Package and verify Kubernetes delivery](#tar-017) - 📋 [TAR-018 — Measure and present the portfolio release](#tar-018) - 🚧 [TAR-019 — Evaluate the multi-agent implement/review orchestrator](#tar-019) ## Delivery notes M2 re-review findings are remediated and verified (both follow-up probes pass; see the [review](evidence/m2/m2-independent-review.md)). Independent M3 re-review of `f9f21df` found F1–F4; all resolved and re-verified (13/13 preserved probes pass). Next action: close the remaining F2 cutover race in TAR-011/TAR-012 before M4. Later tasks remain Backlog until their dependencies and detailed contracts are ready. Portal/API slices can develop alongside their backend tasks; TAR-009 and TAR-012 own integrated acceptance. Observability hooks and correctness tests accompany implementation; TAR-016 owns the full cross-service campaign, not the first tests. The architecture and functional scope are the planning baseline; exact schemas, dependency versions and open profiles are refined in their named tasks. Split large tasks into new IDs before starting if necessary; preserve existing history. Next unused ID: TAR-020. M1 remains verified; M2 remediation is re-verified. Re-review of `db18588` found one remaining F2 commit-window race; resolved by a shared cohort advisory-lock protocol between cutover and all gate-affecting writers — see the [third remediation addendum](evidence/m3/m3-independent-review.md#third-remediation-addendum--2026-10-25). ## TAR-001 — Establish project-management standards - Repository: taryx - Area: documentation - Milestone: Documentation setup - Priority: High - Status: Done ✅ - Depends on: None - References: [Contract](documentation-guide.md) ### Outcome Adapt Cateniq’s portable workflow without copying project history. ### Done when - Root instructions, portable skill and guide agree on ownership, statuses, UTC journal attribution and atomic records updates. - README remains intact apart from navigation/status clarification; local links and UTF-8 checks pass. ### Completion evidence Documentation deliverables created; local link/anchor, dependency, status/index and UTF-8 checks recorded in the [journal](journal/2026-10.md). Files are uncommitted. No application checks apply. ### Notes Use this workflow for subsequent meaningful work. ## TAR-002 — Establish the planning baseline - Repository: taryx - Area: documentation - Milestone: Planning baseline - Priority: High - Status: Done ✅ - Depends on: TAR-001 - References: [Contract](architecture.md) ### Outcome Produce a coherent architecture, staged roadmap, feature contracts and initial task sequence. ### Done when - Architecture separates accepted direction from implementation; features define failure and acceptance cases. - Milestones have dependencies/exclusions/exits; bounded open gates have owners and unblock actions. - Task/index/dependency/link consistency checks pass; no runtime completion is claimed. ### Completion evidence Documentation deliverables created; local link/anchor, dependency, status/index and UTF-8 checks recorded in the [journal](journal/2026-10.md). Files are uncommitted. No application checks apply. ### Notes Next action: TAR-003; domain profile research can begin alongside bootstrap. ## TAR-003 — Bootstrap the development workspace - Repository: taryx - Area: workspace - Milestone: M1 - Priority: High - Status: Done ✅ - Depends on: TAR-002 - References: [Contract](architecture.md) ### Outcome Create a minimal reproducible API, worker and portal skeleton with real PostgreSQL/RabbitMQ. ### Done when - Select compatible supported Python/Django/Graphene/Celery and frontend versions from primary documentation; pin/lock dependencies. - Compose starts API, worker, database and broker; portal connects to a smoke query; startup/config errors are clear. - Import Linter enforces layer/independence/core-interface contracts and rejects a deliberate violation. - Minimal CI configuration and locally executed checks cover formatting, typing where useful, tests and import contracts; hosted status is reported separately. - Document tested install/start/check/reset commands and persistent-volume boundaries. ### Completion evidence - Pinned Python 3.14 / Django 6.1.2 / graphene-django 3.2.3 / Celery 5.6.3 / psycopg 3.3.6 via uv.lock; React 19.3.1 / Vite 8.3.5 / TypeScript 7.0.2 via package-lock.json. - `make check` green locally: ruff lint+format, mypy (django-stubs), 5 pytest tests against real PostgreSQL 18.6, import-contract check, web typecheck+build. - `scripts/check-import-boundaries.sh`: 3 contracts KEPT; deliberate core→interfaces probe rejected. - Compose stack verified running: `/healthz` ok, GraphQL `ping`/`version` via API and via portal Vite proxy, `taryx.smoke.ping` task executed on worker through RabbitMQ 4.3.7. - Host ports offset (db 55432, amqp 5673, mgmt 15673, api 8001, web 5174) to coexist with sibling stacks; # Devin-driven Codex review loop (simplified process)

Status: pilot convention, agreed 2026-11-08; revised same day after a
Codex self-audit (`codex-review-loop-audit.md` — its findings are
adopted selectively here; recommendations there are not all binding).
Predecessors: `multi-agent-handoff-problem.md` (problem framing),
`multi-agent-orchestrator-research.md` (what takt/ccbridge do).

## Purpose

Run a milestone's implement/review cycle with one human "go" message
instead of the user relaying "Devin has done M{N}, can you review" /
"Codex reviewed, can you resolve" between the two desktop apps.

Devin (this Devin Desktop session) is the loop driver. Codex runs as a
synchronous subprocess invoked through its CLI against the **existing**
review thread, so review context accumulates across milestones.

## Actors and mechanism

- **Implementer / driver**: Devin, inside this Devin Desktop session.
  Implements, commits, remediates, and invokes the reviewer.
- **Reviewer**: a dedicated Codex *exec session* per milestone, invoked
  via `codex exec resume <session-id>` from
  `/usr/lib/chatgpt/resources/codex`. A fresh session is created for
  each milestone and resumed across that milestone's remediation
  rounds — a perpetual thread accumulates bias toward its own earlier
  verdicts and compacts away qualifications, so context beyond one
  milestone lives in the repo (review docs, probes), not the session.
  (The desktop-app thread `Taryx project review`,
  `01a16e5a-546f-7850-8796-1484463b943f`, was evaluated and rejected —
  its managed profile is read-only; see "Reviewer permissions".)
- **Mutual exclusion**: between the two agents, structural — while
  `codex exec` runs, Devin is blocked waiting on the subprocess. This
  is *not* an OS lock: other processes (a human editor, a second
  `codex` attach) can still touch the tree. The git-state gate in step
  2 is what detects outside interference.
- **Turn boundary**: the `codex exec` process exit.

### Hard thread rule

`codex exec resume` fails with `thread ... already has an active writer`
if the session is held open elsewhere — e.g. the thread open in the
Codex desktop app, or another `codex` process attached to it. During a
loop run the review session must not be open anywhere else; on a lock
conflict Devin stops and asks rather than retrying.

## The loop

For each milestone M{N}, after implementation and its commit:

1. **Review invocation** — Devin runs:

   ```bash
   /usr/lib/chatgpt/resources/codex exec -C "$REPO" --approve-for-me \
     resume <session-id> \
     --output-schema docs/project/evidence/verdict.schema.json \
     --json \
     -o docs/project/evidence/m{N}-verdict-r{R}.json \
     "M{N} implementation is committed at <sha>. Review per our
      conventions: write findings to
      docs/project/evidence/m{N}-independent-review.md plus runnable
      pytest probes, and update affected project records. Do not
      commit."
   ```

   Exec-level options (`-C`, `--approve-for-me`, `-c`) go **before**
   `resume` — they are not resume's own options. `--json` tees the
   event stream to stdout (capture it into
   `m{N}-events-r{R}.jsonl`); `--output-schema` constrains the final
   message, which `-o` saves — the verdict is a JSON artifact, not a
   prose marker. The human-readable review lives in the repo files
   Codex writes, not in `-o`.

   The review session is provisioned **once per milestone**, before
   its first round:

   ```bash
   /usr/lib/chatgpt/resources/codex exec -C "$REPO" --approve-for-me \
     -c 'sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true' \
     "You are the independent reviewer for Taryx milestone M{N}.
      Review conventions live in docs/project/documentation-guide.md
      and docs/agent-notes/. Reply READY." \
     -o docs/project/evidence/m{N}-session-bootstrap.md
   ```

   Record the new session id (from the `--json` event stream or
   `session_index.jsonl`) in `handoff/state` or the journal — never
   use `--last` in automation.

   `--approve-for-me` selects workspace-write plus automatic review of
   approval requests. Verified 2026-11-08: sandboxed file writes work
   on both the create call and later `exec resume` rounds, and the
   audit run itself wrote docs/backlog/journal inside this repo.
   Whether automatic *escalation* (approval requests above the
   sandbox) survives resume is unverified — `approval_policy` drops
   to `never` on resume, which means "cannot ask", not "approve all".
   `network_access=true` enables broad command networking (not just
   localhost) and is needed for the dockerised Postgres on
   localhost:55432 — DB reachability on resume still needs a live
   round.

   Long reviews run as a backgrounded exec; Devin polls until exit.
   Record `git rev-parse HEAD` **and** `git status --porcelain`
   before the call.

2. **Gate checks on exit** — Devin verifies:

   - HEAD unchanged *and* the working tree matches its pre-call state
     except for allowed paths (`docs/`, probe files, `handoff/`).
     An unchanged HEAD does **not** prove the source is unchanged —
     staged, unstaged, and untracked writes must all be checked, and
     unexpected-path writes make the round fail, not approved.
   - The verdict JSON parses against the schema **and** its semantics:
     `reviewed_sha` equals the candidate SHA, verdict ∈
     `APPROVED | CHANGES_REQUESTED | BLOCKED`, required checks are
     present. `APPROVED` with missing checks or a SHA mismatch is
     rejected — schema compliance is not review correctness.
   - A crash, timeout, missing verdict, or unexpected write counts as
     an incomplete round, not an approval.

3. **Commit the docs first** — Codex's working-tree output (review doc,
   probes, record updates) is reviewed by Devin and committed as the
   first step of remediation, per the existing convention.

4. **Remediation** — if `CHANGES_REQUESTED`: Devin resolves findings,
   folds probes into the test suite, commits, then re-invokes step 1
   for the next round. The resumed thread carries prior-round context.

5. **Termination** — proceed to the next milestone only on
   `verdict: APPROVED` in the schema output **and** the preserved
   probes plus required project checks green. `BLOCKED` also ends the
   loop — straight to escalation.

6. **Escalation** — stop to the user after **3 rounds** without
   approval, on `verdict: BLOCKED`, or on any ambiguous state (lock
   conflict, unparsable verdict, unexpected writes, Codex blocked
   needing input). Do not loop indefinitely; an authorized extra round
   is recorded in loop state, not just conversation.

## Standing rules (unchanged)

- Devin makes every commit; Codex makes none.
- `git push` is always manual — never prompted, never run by the loop.
- Review docs, preserved probes, and record updates follow
  `docs/project/documentation-guide.md`.

## Reviewer permissions

Observed 2026-11-08 (M3 loop, rounds 1–4): the `Taryx project review`
desktop thread runs a **managed restricted** profile — filesystem
read-only, `network: restricted`, `approval_policy: never`, and `cwd`
pinned to an unrelated project directory. It could source-review and
report findings via `-o`, but could not write docs/probes or run the
database tests.

**Why interactive chat feels fully-permitted**: the app thread answers
approval requests through `approvals_reviewer: auto_review` — an
automated reviewer grants scoped elevation per action. That is the
same thing `--approve-for-me` selects on the CLI; it is *not* the
`--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` mode.

**Why `exec resume` on that thread is read-only**: resume inherits the
*session's* profile. "Managed" does not prove every override is
ignored — admin requirements constrain overrides, but exact precedence
for that thread is unverified. The reliable fix is to resume a session
that was *created* with a writable profile.

Verified 2026-11-08 on this machine:

- `codex exec --approve-for-me` → `approval: on-request` (routed to
  auto-review), `sandbox: workspace-write [workdir, /tmp, $TMPDIR]` —
  wrote files and ran commands. The early probes wrote `/tmp` only.
- `codex exec resume <that-session>` → keeps `workspace-write`,
  `approval: never` — wrote files with no flags needed.
- The self-audit run (`codex exec -C taryx --approve-for-me
  -c 'sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true'`) wrote
  `codex-review-loop-audit.md`, backlog, and journal entries directly
  into this repo — first live *repo* write evidence, not just `/tmp`.
- Still unverified: approval escalation above the sandbox on resume,
  and Postgres connectivity through the resumed session.

Options, in preference order:

1. **Dedicated exec session per milestone (adopted)** — fresh session
   per milestone, resumed across that milestone's rounds.
   Write/exec verified including repo paths. Not an app thread, so the
   writer-lock rule does not apply.
2. **New chat in the Codex "Taryx" project** on a trusted, writable
   project profile — equivalent permissions via the app profile, plus
   the transcript stays in the desktop UI. Writer-lock rule applies.
3. **`--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`** — disables Codex
   sandboxing and confirmations *where permitted*; it does not
   override OS, container, or admin-enforced restrictions. Emergency
   only — not required for the ordinary loop.
4. **Fallback (verified)** — restricted thread + `-o` verdict `.md`
   committed as the review artifact; Devin authors record updates.

## Known limitations

- **Thread lock**: app-open thread breaks `exec resume` (above).
- **Context growth**: resumed threads compact over many milestones; if
  the reviewer loses conventions, pin the review prompt text above or
  fall back to stateless rounds with the review doc as the contract.
- **No independent check on Devin**: the loop verifies Codex's output
  mechanically (HEAD, verdict file, probes) but Devin's own gates are
  self-enforced. Human review of commits before push remains the
  backstop.
- **`codex queue --thread` exists** for injecting messages while the
  app holds the thread, but delivery is async — not used by this loop.

## Human touchpoints per milestone

1. "Go on M{N}" — one message starts the whole cycle.
2. Escalations, if any (round cap, lock, blocked reviewer).
3. Review the commits and push manually when satisfied.

"""Billing admission, outbox processing and atomic issuance.

Admission is durable before any task dispatch: the operation and its
outbox event commit together, so broker downtime never loses intent and
at-least-once processing is safe. Issuance is one transaction: staleness
precondition, numbered invoice, balanced journal and operation/outbox
completion — or nothing at all.
"""

import hashlib
import os
from collections.abc import Callable
from decimal import Decimal

from django.db import connection, transaction
from django.db.models import Sum
from django.db.utils import IntegrityError
from django.utils import timezone

from taryx.core.accounts.models import Account
from taryx.core.billing.models import (
    Adjustment,
    BillingOperation,
    Invoice,
    JournalEntry,
    OutboxEvent,
    Posting,
)
from taryx.core.pricing.models import RatingRun
from taryx.core.pricing.services import lock_inputs

# Minimal fictional-retailer chart of accounts (billing subledger).
ACC_RECEIVABLE = "1100"
ACC_GST_LIABILITY = "2100"
ACC_ENERGY_REVENUE = "4000"
ACC_EXPORT_CREDIT = "4100"

TOPIC_ISSUE = "billing.issue"


class AdmissionError(ValueError):
    def __init__(self, code: str, detail: str):
        self.code = code
        super().__init__(detail)


class CalculationUnavailable(Exception):
    """The pinned authoritative engine could not produce a result.

    Transient by definition: the operation stays PENDING (in-flight) so
    it also blocks cohort mode changes until it resolves or is replaced.
    """

    def __init__(self, code: str, detail: str):
        self.code = code
        super().__init__(detail)


def _payload_sha(
    account: Account,
    period_start,
    period_end,
    rating_run: RatingRun,
    cohort_mode: str,
    cohort_revision: int,
) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(
        f"{account.reference}|{period_start}|{period_end}|{rating_run.id}"
        f"|{cohort_mode}|{cohort_revision}".encode()
    ).hexdigest()


def admit_issue(
    account: Account,
    period_start,
    period_end,
    rating_run: RatingRun,
    operation_id: str,
    *,
    routing_resolver=None,
) -> BillingOperation:
    """Durably admit a billing operation and its outbox event atomically.

    Processing routes on billed state: the first operation for a period
    issues the invoice; a later operation pinned to a different input
    digest posts a linked adjustment instead. The caller may enqueue a
    fast-path task afterwards; if the broker is down the pending outbox
    event is recovered by drain_outbox.

    The routing pin is resolved under the account row lock: the lock
    conflicts with a cohort cutover's member locks, so an admission can
    never pin a routing identity after the cutover's final pending-ops
    check but before the route commit.
    """
    try:
        with transaction.atomic():
            Account.objects.select_for_update().get(pk=account.pk)
            if routing_resolver is None:
                cohort_mode, cohort_revision = "new_only", 0
            else:
                cohort_mode, cohort_revision = routing_resolver(account)
            payload = _payload_sha(
                account,
                period_start,
                period_end,
                rating_run,
                cohort_mode,
                cohort_revision,
            )
            op = BillingOperation.objects.create(
                operation_id=operation_id,
                account=account,
                period_start=period_start,
                period_end=period_end,
                rating_run=rating_run,
                payload_sha256=payload,
                cohort_mode=cohort_mode,
                cohort_revision=cohort_revision,
            )
            OutboxEvent.objects.create(operation=op, topic=TOPIC_ISSUE)
        return op
    except IntegrityError:
        # Loser of a concurrent same-key admission: resolve the winner.
        existing = BillingOperation.objects.get(operation_id=operation_id)
        if existing.payload_sha256 != payload:
            raise AdmissionError(
                "operation_conflict",
                f"operation {operation_id!r} already admitted with a different payload",
            ) from None
        return existing


def _next_number(sequence: str, prefix: str) -> str:
    with connection.cursor() as cursor:
        cursor.execute(f"SELECT nextval('{sequence}')")
        (value,) = cursor.fetchone()
    return f"{prefix}-{value:06d}"


def _run_amounts(run: RatingRun) -> dict[str, Decimal]:
    """Element-level monetary result of a rating run."""
    zero = type(run.net)(0)
    return {
        "charge": sum(
            (line.amount for line in run.lines.all() if line.element in {"import", "supply"}),
            start=zero,
        ),
        "export": -sum(
            (line.amount for line in run.lines.all() if line.element == "export_credit"),
            start=zero,
        ),
        "gst": run.gst,
        "net": run.net,
        "total": run.total,
    }


def _recognised_amounts(invoice: Invoice) -> dict[str, Decimal]:
    """Liability already recognised by every journal posted to an invoice.

    The ledger is the source of truth: revenue/GST legs are credit-positive,
    receivable/export legs debit-positive."""
    legs = (
        Posting.objects.filter(journal__invoice=invoice)
        .values("account_code")
        .annotate(dr=Sum("debit"), cr=Sum("credit"))
    )
    zero = Decimal(0)
    balance = {row["account_code"]: (row["dr"] or zero) - (row["cr"] or zero) for row in legs}
    return {
        "charge": -balance.get(ACC_ENERGY_REVENUE, zero),
        "export": balance.get(ACC_EXPORT_CREDIT, zero),
        "gst": -balance.get(ACC_GST_LIABILITY, zero),
        "total": balance.get(ACC_RECEIVABLE, zero),
    }


def _leg(journal: JournalEntry, code: str, debit, credit, memo: str) -> Posting | None:
    if not debit and not credit:
        return None
    return Posting(journal=journal, account_code=code, debit=debit, credit=credit, memo=memo)


def _signed_leg(journal: JournalEntry, code: str, delta: Decimal, memo: str) -> Posting | None:
    """One leg per element; a negative amount swaps the side so net-credit
    bills (export exceeding charges) post to the correct ledger side."""
    return _leg(journal, code, max(delta, 0), max(-delta, 0), memo)


def _authoritative_amounts(op: BillingOperation, legacy_calculator) -> dict[str, Decimal]:
    """Amounts per the op's pinned routing mode: under legacy_only/shadow
    the legacy calculator is authoritative; otherwise the rating run."""
    if op.cohort_mode in {"legacy_only", "shadow"}:
        if legacy_calculator is None:
            raise CalculationUnavailable(
                "no_calculator", "no legacy calculator configured for legacy routing"
            )
        return legacy_calculator(op)
    return _run_amounts(op.rating_run)


def _issue(op: BillingOperation, amounts: dict[str, Decimal]) -> Invoice:
    run = op.rating_run
    invoice = Invoice.objects.create(
        number=_next_number("billing_invoice_number_seq", "INV"),
        account=op.account,
        period_start=op.period_start,
        period_end=op.period_end,
        rating_run=run,
        input_digest=run.input_digest,
        calculation_source=_op_source(op),
        net=amounts["net"],
        gst=amounts["gst"],
        total=amounts["total"],
    )
    journal = JournalEntry.objects.create(
        invoice=invoice,
        operation=op,
        memo=f"{invoice.number} {op.account.reference} {op.period_start}..{op.period_end}",
    )
    postings = [
        _signed_leg(journal, ACC_RECEIVABLE, amounts["total"], f"receivable {invoice.number}"),
        _signed_leg(
            journal, ACC_ENERGY_REVENUE, -amounts["charge"], f"energy+supply {invoice.number}"
        ),
        _signed_leg(
            journal, ACC_EXPORT_CREDIT, amounts["export"], f"feed-in credit {invoice.number}"
        ),
        _signed_leg(journal, ACC_GST_LIABILITY, -amounts["gst"], f"gst {invoice.number}"),
    ]
    Posting.objects.bulk_create(p for p in postings if p is not None)
    return invoice


def _op_source(op: BillingOperation) -> str:
    return "legacy" if op.cohort_mode in {"legacy_only", "shadow"} else "new"


def _post_correction(
    op: BillingOperation, invoice: Invoice, generation: int, revised: dict[str, Decimal]
) -> Adjustment:
    """Append a linked adjustment reconciling the revised calculation
    against the liability already recognised on this invoice (invoice
    row lock held)."""
    run = op.rating_run
    recognised = _recognised_amounts(invoice)
    delta = {key: revised[key] - recognised[key] for key in recognised}
    adjustment = Adjustment.objects.create(
        number=_next_number("billing_adjustment_number_seq", "ADJ"),
        invoice=invoice,
        rating_run=run,
        input_digest=run.input_digest,
        calculation_source=_op_source(op),
        generation=generation,
        delta_charge=delta["charge"],
        delta_export=delta["export"],
        delta_gst=delta["gst"],
        delta_total=delta["total"],
    )
    if any(delta.values()):
        journal = JournalEntry.objects.create(
            invoice=invoice,
            adjustment=adjustment,
            operation=op,
            memo=f"{adjustment.number} correction for {invoice.number}",

            _signed_leg(journal, ACC_RECEIVABLE, delta["total"], "receivable"),
            _signed_leg(journal, ACC_ENERGY_REVENUE, -delta["charge"], "energy+supply"),

def _finish(op: BillingOperation, status: str, detail: str = "") -> BillingOperation:
    op.status = status
    op.detail = detail
    op.completed_at = timezone.now()
    op.save(update_fields=["status", "detail", "completed_at", "invoice", "adjustment"])
    op.outbox_event.delivered_at = op.completed_at
    op.outbox_event.save(update_fields=["delivered_at"])
    return op


def process_operation(
    operation_id: str,
    *,
    digest_resolver: Callable[[Account, object, object], str],
    routing_resolver: Callable[[Account], tuple[str, int]] | None = None,
    legacy_calculator: Callable[[BillingOperation], dict] | None = None,
) -> BillingOperation:
    """Process one admitted operation idempotently under its row lock.

    Routes on the billed state of the account/period: no invoice issues
    one; an invoice with a different pinned digest posts a linked
    adjustment against the recognised generation. The invoice row lock
    serializes adjustment generations so concurrent revisions and stale
    calculations cannot supersede the newest recognised run."""
    with transaction.atomic():
        op = BillingOperation.objects.select_for_update().get(operation_id=operation_id)
        if op.status != BillingOperation.Status.PENDING:
            return op  # duplicate delivery is a no-op

        if digest_resolver(op.account, op.period_start, op.period_end) != (
            op.rating_run.input_digest
        ):
            return _finish(
                op,
                BillingOperation.Status.STALE,
                "input selection changed since the pinned rating run",
            )

        # Routing pin re-check: the cohort mode/revision this op was
        # admitted under must still be current. (Mode changes are already
        # blocked while ops are pending; this guard also catches a cohort
        # membership adopted after admission.)
        if routing_resolver is not None:
            current_mode, current_revision = routing_resolver(op.account)
            if (current_mode, current_revision) != (
                op.cohort_mode,
                op.cohort_revision,
            ):
                return _finish(
                    op,
                    BillingOperation.Status.STALE,
                    "cohort routing changed since admission",
                )

        # Under legacy routing the authoritative amounts come from a
        # remote call that also writes shadow-alias evidence. It must run
        # BEFORE lock_inputs: the shadow connection's FK checks wait on
        # FOR UPDATE locks held by this transaction (account lock →
        # deadlock the database cannot detect cross-connection).
        amounts = _authoritative_amounts(op, legacy_calculator)

        # Commit-safe revalidation: lock the account and every row feeding
        # the digest, then recompute under those locks. Any input change
        # committed meanwhile is now visible (stale); a change still in
        # flight either already holds these locks (we wait, then see it) or
        # blocks on the account lock it must take before mutating, so it
        # can only land after this transaction commits. The digest also
        # covers open quarantines, which input locks alone cannot pin.
        lock_inputs(op.account, op.period_start, op.period_end)
        # Routing pin re-check under the input locks: a cutover committed
        # while this transaction waited on the account lock must not
        # issue under the admitted legacy pin.
        if routing_resolver is not None:
            current_mode, current_revision = routing_resolver(op.account)
            if (current_mode, current_revision) != (
                op.cohort_mode,
                op.cohort_revision,
            ):
                return _finish(
                    op,
                    BillingOperation.Status.STALE,
                    "cohort routing changed during issuance validation",
                )
        if digest_resolver(op.account, op.period_start, op.period_end) != (
            op.rating_run.input_digest
        ):
            return _finish(
                op,
                BillingOperation.Status.STALE,
                "inputs changed during issuance validation",
            )

        invoice = (
            Invoice.objects.select_for_update()
            .filter(
                account=op.account,
                period_start=op.period_start,
                period_end=op.period_end,
            )
            .order_by("id")
            .first()
        )
        if invoice is None:
            try:
                with transaction.atomic():
                    invoice = _issue(op, amounts)
            except IntegrityError as exc:
                # Only the generation-key uniqueness violation means a
                # racing issuance already posted; anything else is a real
                # failure and must surface rather than hang the operation.
                if "uniq_bill_generation" not in str(exc):
                    raise
                invoice = Invoice.objects.get(
                    account=op.account,
                    period_start=op.period_start,
                    period_end=op.period_end,
                    input_digest=op.rating_run.input_digest,
                )
            op.invoice = invoice
        else:
            run = op.rating_run
            latest = invoice.adjustments.order_by("-generation").first()
            recognised = latest or invoice
            op_source = _op_source(op)
            same_source = recognised.calculation_source == op_source
            if recognised.input_digest == run.input_digest and same_source:
                # Repeat of the currently recognised generation — same
                # inputs under the same authoritative engine.
                op.invoice = invoice
                op.adjustment = latest
            elif run.id <= recognised.rating_run_id and same_source:
                return _finish(
                    op,
                    BillingOperation.Status.STALE,
                    "calculation superseded by a newer recognised generation",
                )
            else:
                op.invoice = invoice
                op.adjustment = _post_correction(
                    op,
                    invoice,
                    generation=(latest.generation if latest else 0) + 1,
                    revised=amounts,
                )

        _finish(op, BillingOperation.Status.COMPLETE)
        if os.environ.get("TARYX_BILLING_CRASH") == "before_commit":
            os._exit(1)  # test-only crash point: die before the txn commits
    return op


def drain_outbox(
    *,
    digest_resolver: Callable[[Account, object, object], str],
    routing_resolver: Callable[[Account], tuple[str, int]] | None = None,
    legacy_calculator: Callable[[BillingOperation], dict] | None = None,
    limit: int = 200,
) -> list[BillingOperation]:
    """Recover pending outbox events (broker outage, lost tasks)."""
    pending = list(
        OutboxEvent.objects.filter(delivered_at__isnull=True)
        .order_by("created_at")
        .values_list("operation__operation_id", flat=True)[:limit]
    )
    return [
        process_operation(
            operation_id,
            digest_resolver=digest_resolver,
            routing_resolver=routing_resolver,
            legacy_calculator=legacy_calculator,
        )
        for operation_id in pending
    ]

    same payload returns this row; the same id with a different payload is
    a conflict rejected at admission.

    class Status(models.TextChoices):
        PENDING = "pending"
        COMPLETE = "complete"
        STALE = "stale"

    operation_id = models.CharField(max_length=64, unique=True)
    account = models.ForeignKey(Account, on_delete=models.PROTECT, related_name="billing_ops")
    period_start = models.DateField()
    period_end = models.DateField()
    rating_run = models.ForeignKey(RatingRun, on_delete=models.PROTECT, related_name="billing_ops")
    payload_sha256 = models.CharField(max_length=64)
    # Cohort routing pinned at admission (resolved by the caller — billing
    # stays unaware of the migration app): which engine is authoritative
    # for this op and which routing revision it was admitted under.
    cohort_mode = models.CharField(max_length=16, default="new_only")

    status = models.CharField(max_length=16, choices=Status.choices, default=Status.PENDING)
    invoice = models.ForeignKey(

    )

        "Adjustment", null=True, blank=True, on_delete=models.PROTECT, related_name="+"
    )
    detail = models.TextField(blank=True)
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)
    completed_at = models.DateTimeField(null=True)


class OutboxEvent(models.Model):

    operation = models.OneToOneField(

    number = models.CharField(max_length=20, unique=True)

@pytest.mark.django_db(transaction=True)
def test_racing_operations_cannot_double_issue():
    seed_demo_data()
    ingest_nem12_content(load("day1_base.nem12"), "day1_base.nem12")
    account = Account.objects.get(reference="ACC-001")
    run = rate_account(account, DAY, NEXT, **KWARGS)
    ops = [admit(account, run, f"OP-R{i}") for i in range(2)]
    barrier = Barrier(2)
    original = billing_services.lock_inputs

    def gated_lock(*args):
        # Both operations pass validation together, then race for the
        # account lock that serialises input validation through commit.
        barrier.wait(timeout=10)
        return original(*args)

    def go(op):
        close_old_connections()
        try:
            process(op)
        finally:
            close_old_connections()

    with (
        patch.object(billing_services, "lock_inputs", gated_lock),
        ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) as pool,
    ):
        futures = [pool.submit(go, op) for op in ops]
        for f in futures:
            f.result(timeout=30)
    assert Invoice.objects.count() == 1
    invoice = Invoice.objects.get()
    assert {BillingOperation.objects.get(pk=o.pk).invoice_id for o in ops} == {invoice.id}
    assert {BillingOperation.objects.get(pk=o.pk).status for o in ops} == {"complete"}

    invoice = process(admit(account, run)).invoice
    journal = invoice.journal_entries.get()
    posting = journal.postings.first()

    with pytest.raises(DbError, match="immutable"), transaction.atomic():
        Invoice.objects.filter(pk=invoice.pk).update(total=0)
    # Raw SQL bypasses ORM PROTECT: the database trigger itself must reject.
    with (
        pytest.raises(DbError, match="immutable"),
        transaction.atomic(),
        connection.cursor() as cursor,

    with pytest.raises(DbError, match="immutable"), transaction.atomic():
        JournalEntry.objects.filter(pk=journal.pk).update(memo="tampered")
    with pytest.raises(DbError, match="immutable"), transaction.atomic():
        posting.delete()

def test_unbalanced_journal_rejected_at_commit():

    ingest_nem12_content(load("day1_base.nem12"), "day1_base.nem12")

### F1 — Medium: Empty journal headers bypass the database balance invariant

Location: `src/taryx/core/billing/migrations/0002_financial_integrity.py:44` (posting-only deferred trigger); `JournalEntry` creation.

The deferred check is scheduled only when a posting changes. Creating a journal header without any postings commits successfully, despite the documented minimum of two balanced postings. The journal then seals at commit and cannot receive its missing legs. This leaves an immutable, permanently incomplete financial journal. It also means an issuing path that accidentally omits all legs can evade the claimed database guard.

The independent probe creates a journal for an issued invoice inside a real committed transaction and expects an IntegrityError. PostgreSQL accepts it. Add a deferred check on journal creation as well as posting changes, inspecting the final posting set; preserve valid multi-leg transactions and explicitly decide any zero-value journal policy. Owner: TAR-007. This is the empty-journal case requested by historical M2 R4 but absent from its remediation tests.

### F2 — High: A failing outbox event prevents later independent recovery

Location: `src/taryx/core/billing/services.py:437–450`.

The drain selects oldest pending events and processes them in a list comprehension. Any calculation/service exception aborts the drain before later events run. The failing event stays pending and is selected first again on every invocation. After lost task delivery or a broker outage, one unavailable legacy calculation can therefore indefinitely prevent healthy new-engine billing from recovering, even though its inputs and calculator are available. Durable storage alone does not provide recovery progress.

The independent probe admits an unavailable legacy operation followed by a healthy new-engine operation. Two drains both encounter the same synthetic CalculationUnavailable; the healthy operation remains pending. Isolate failures per event and retain observable retry state; ensure a full batch of failing older events cannot permanently starve later work (for example with bounded retry scheduling). Do not mark unsuccessful work delivered. Owner: TAR-007; recovery campaign follow-up TAR-016.

### F3 — Medium: The operator cannot inspect bill line-item provenance

Location: `web/src/App.tsx:429–454` (issued documents) and the AccountPanel rating/invoice queries.

The portal displays the invoice total and ledger account debits/credits, plus adjustment total deltas. It does not fetch or render the immutable rating lines, quantities, unit rates, tariff/period provenance or calculation explanation for the selected invoice. Operators cannot perform the specified import/bill/**explain**/correct journey: ledger legs do not explain how metered usage became a charge. ## Findings

### F1 — Medium: Empty journal headers bypass the database balance invariant

Location: `src/taryx/core/billing/migrations/0002_financial_integrity.py:44` (posting-only deferred trigger); `JournalEntry` creation.

The deferred check is scheduled only when a posting changes. Creating a journal header without any postings commits successfully, despite the documented minimum of two balanced postings. The journal then seals at commit and cannot receive its missing legs. This leaves an immutable, permanently incomplete financial journal. It also means an issuing path that accidentally omits all legs can evade the claimed database guard.

The independent probe creates a journal for an issued invoice inside a real committed transaction and expects an IntegrityError. PostgreSQL accepts it. Add a deferred check on journal creation as well as posting changes, inspecting the final posting set; preserve valid multi-leg transactions and explicitly decide any zero-value journal policy. Owner: TAR-007. This is the empty-journal case requested by historical M2 R4 but absent from its remediation tests.

### F2 — High: A failing outbox event prevents later independent recovery

Location: `src/taryx/core/billing/services.py:437–450`.

The drain selects oldest pending events and processes them in a list comprehension. Any calculation/service exception aborts the drain before later events run. The failing event stays pending and is selected first again on every invocation. After lost task delivery or a broker outage, one unavailable legacy calculation can therefore indefinitely prevent healthy new-engine billing from recovering, even though its inputs and calculator are available. Durable storage alone does not provide recovery progress.

The independent probe admits an unavailable legacy operation followed by a healthy new-engine operation. Two drains both encounter the same synthetic CalculationUnavailable; the healthy operation remains pending. Isolate failures per event and retain observable retry state; ensure a full batch of failing older events cannot permanently starve later work (for example with bounded retry scheduling). Do not mark unsuccessful work delivered. Owner: TAR-007; recovery campaign follow-up TAR-016.

### F3 — Medium: The operator cannot inspect bill line-item provenance

Location: `web/src/App.tsx:429–454` (issued documents) and the AccountPanel rating/invoice queries.

The portal displays the invoice total and ledger account debits/credits, plus adjustment total deltas. It does not fetch or render the immutable rating lines, quantities, unit rates, tariff/period provenance or calculation explanation for the selected invoice. Operators cannot perform the specified import/bill/**explain**/correct journey: ledger legs do not explain how metered usage became a charge. The accepted operator contract explicitly requires bill/line-item provenance and browser bill explanation. This is the residual itemised-portal gap already identified in the historical M2 review, now confirmed by source inspection rather than treated as completed.
